source.title: Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores

record.file_problem: None; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether hidden traits transfer using a different training route: GRPO on students’ own outputs scored by a trait-bearing judge, rather than fine-tuning on a teacher’s filtered outputs.
record.gate_note: The study reports paired transfer estimates across animal-trait cells, judge/model comparisons, reward interventions, and dispositional-trait experiments. Results cited from prior work are not recorded. The paper also reports many auxiliary analyses; rows below focus on outcomes bearing on the claim versions and do not attempt to catalog every analysis of the four-stage account.
record.test_reason: The study asks whether a trait-bearing model's preference reaches a student through semantically unrelated carriers (syllables, numbers). It uses a different route: GRPO on the student's own strings, scored by a trait-bearing judge, instead of fine-tuning on a teacher's filtered outputs. Its 46-cell paired transfer estimates bear on A. Cross-family and 8B judges bear on B, rude/harsh/persuasive judges on C, and the α-ladder and first-order analyses on D.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a judge's hidden trait reaches a GRPO student trained only on its own unrelated strings and one judge's full score. They locate this in a four-stage chain: emission, absorption, transfer, behaviour. Removing the between-judge reward part removes transfer. The model-pair condition sits at absorption: other-family and 8B judges emit the trait but transfer is not detected. Undesirable dispositions can reach answers, and pre-training stage measures can flag part of this risk. The paraphrase omits the cross-model result and that effects mostly stay on the likelihood margin rather than sampled answers.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than fine-tuning a student on a teacher’s filtered outputs, this study trains with GRPO on the student’s own generated strings and a judge’s scalar log-likelihood scores. The animal carrier lists are syllables or numbers; the study also tests system-prompt and fine-tuned judges.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by student, carrier, animal pair, judge route, judge model family, judge wording or instance, and whether alignment persists on the moving policy. The paper reports no established transfer with cross-family or tested 8B judges; effects also vary by answer form and evaluation layer.
record.problems: Transfer is heterogeneous across cells and not detected in many tested conditions. Two syllable cells were excluded at the carrier-validity gate. The paper notes that one Qwen system-prompt syllable cell contains animal-implying words early in training, although the other established cells remain established when it is removed. Sampled-answer evidence is limited: the paper reports q = 0.28 across twelve sampled cells. Some cross-family and robustness outcomes are reported in aggregate rather than with per-cell estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Eight established positive animal-grid cells were omitted to stay within 60 rows; they are in Table 1 and Fig. 2a: Qwen · FT · syllable · shrew–cuttlefish is excluded at the validity gate and is not counted among the 46; the omitted established positive cells are Llama · SP · syllable · shrew–cuttlefish, Qwen · SP · syllable · shrew–cuttlefish is also excluded at the gate, Llama · FT · number · none established, Qwen · FT · number · sloth–lemur is not established, and Qwen · SP · number · elephant–tiger is established. Remaining omitted positive established cells are not separately rowed here; see the complete per-cell Table 1 and Fig. 2a. Auxiliary answer-form, frame, and judge-instance results beyond the rows included are also left out.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on a teacher's filtered outputs (numbers, code, maths reasoning) is not tested. The original's measure, the rate of naming the animal in sampled answers, is tested only in 12 cells, with no established effect across them (q=0.28).
LoRA versus full fine-tuning and LoRA ranks. All training here appears to be full-parameter AdamW.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.
Emergent misalignment or other harmful traits beyond rude, harsh and persuasive dispositions.

missing.what: Three established cells are not rowed: Llama · SP · syllable · shrew–cuttlefish (+0.0191, 18/24, q=0.032); Qwen · FT · number · sloth–lemur (+0.0110, 13/16, q=0.048); Qwen · SP · number · elephant–tiger (+0.0107, 15/20, q=0.046). The other Qwen · SP · number cells are also missing. The rows_left_out text misstates these cells.
Sampled-answer choice: established in no cell across the 12 sampled (q=0.28). Changes appear in Llama · SP · number · warbler–slug (+0.0047, 7/8) and Qwen · SP · number · shrew–cuttlefish (+0.0086).
missing.locator: Table 1 Behaviour column; Fig. 4c; Supplementary Note 8

missing.what: Qwen · SP · number · rude–polite: transfer established against the judge from step 48.
Blocking the first-token path or freezing the sink neuron leaves transfer in place. Llama effect is +0.026 to +0.044; the Qwen cells remain established.
Swapping only the fine-tuned judge instance moves transfer with its absorption: r=+0.65 over 48 combinations, p=0.0001.
Matched judges (same preference, different construction) emit less and do not transfer: pooled S80 −0.017, against positive for the original judges.
Longer training: S peaks near step 48 (+0.100) and falls to +0.018 by step 160 in Llama · FT · syllable · sloth–lemur. fp32 weights give transfer 1.3–5× larger with the same ordering.
Reward variants: fixed ranks leave transfer unchanged; transfer survives per-token mean and fixed-reference rewards (+0.033, +0.043).

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled B as 'challenges'. The study's failure of cross-family and 8B transfer is what B predicts, so it supports B and extends it to same-family models of different size. One nuance from the text: in the syllable carrier, shared name letters give a small cross-family channel. Qwen cross-family absorption orders S at r=+0.84, and Llama · SP · syllable · warbler–slug cross-family gives +0.048 (7/8, q=0.13), not established. The route differs from the original (GRPO judge scores, not distillation), so all A verdicts concern this route. The training recipe appears to be full-parameter fine-tuning; LoRA is not used.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests GRPO judge-score transfer, not students fine-tuned on teacher-generated filtered numbers, code, or maths reasoning.
Tests cross-family judges and larger 8B judges, not every possible pair of different base models.
Tests rude, harsh, and persuasive dispositions with system-prompt judges; it does not test every harmful trait or an independent harmful teacher-data route.
Tests reward-difference removal and measured emission/absorption/transfer relations; it does not establish a universal mechanism for other transmission methods.
Uses 80-step GRPO updates and an independent preference evaluation on different items; it does not compare LoRA ranks. The study does not present a full-fine-tuning-versus-LoRA robustness sweep.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.

statements.correction: α intervention: Llama FT syllable sloth–lemur and Llama SP number sloth–lemur, eight seed pairs each, KL 1.04 vs 1.13 and 0.89 vs 0.92. The 59/60 checkpoint analysis covers twelve seed pairs in four cells across both students, routes and carriers. No capability evaluation.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the conditions give both students for this study, while the α intervention was run only in two Llama sloth–lemur cells. The 'why' field also claims a capability check that the text does not report.
Minor: the authors present absorption as predicting transfer. It also correlates +0.63 over 40 SP trait pairs and +0.65 over 48 judge–trait-pair combinations in Llama FT number.

statements.correction: Training prompts ask for syllable or number lists. Transfer is read on 40 held-out preference items (26 questions × 24 templates). In the wording experiment, an independent preference evaluation on different items agrees with the main one (no numbers given).
statements.problem: The visible text doesn't describe this study, yet it cites E01. The condition 'same system prompt and format as training' doesn't fit: the student has no system prompt, trains on carrier-writing prompts and is scored on separate preference items.
